items.title: Negaunee council advances zoning limits on data centers
items.dek: Council voted 7-0 to approve the first reading of an ordinance confining data centers to mining and industrial zones, with noise, height and emissions rules. Officials said the restrictions, required by state law against outright bans, could push projects elsewhere.
items.source: Negaunee City Council or Planning Commission agenda
items.findings: Ordinance limits data centers to mining and industrial zones per the draft reviewed by Planning Commission | Requires any air pollution, dust, smoke, glare, exhaust, noise, heat, vibration or humidity to be imperceptible at or beyond the property line | Sets maximum building heights and acceptable noise levels | First reading approved 7-0 by City Council on July 16, 2026 with public hearing set for Aug. 13 | Council members Jon Becker, Amanda Ghanavati and Dave Kangas voiced hope the rules would deter projects | Michigan law outlaws exclusionary zoning, preventing municipalities from completely outlawing specific lawful land-uses including data centers
items.perspective: Negaunee Planning Commission drafted the ordinance and recommended it to City Council last month; City Council advanced the first reading unanimously before scheduling the Aug. 13 hearing. The full ordinance is available in the packet for the July 16 meeting at www.cityofnegaunee.com/city-council/agenda/regular-meeting-45.

items.title: East Lansing extends data center moratorium to March 2027 to develop regulations
items.dek: City Council voted unanimously to prolong the pause, allowing more time for a work group to finalize guidelines amid growing concerns over large-scale projects.
items.judge_note: New council vote extending East Lansing's moratorium to a specific new date (March 2027), a concrete decision distinct from the earlier aquifer-focused pause.
